summary:
On January 8, 2024, at 12:45, Liberty County EMS Rescue 14 was dispatched to the NSK plant for an industrial machinery entrapment involving Jonathan Davis, age 28, whose left arm was crushed by a metal stamping press. A tourniquet was applied by a factory responder and IV Fentanyl 100mcg was administered before transport to Midwest Regional Medical Center. Davis was admitted emergently to ICU-04 at 13:25 with an admitting diagnosis of complete traumatic amputation between the shoulder and elbow, left arm (S48.112A), under attending Dr. Marcus Vance and admitting Dr. David Cho. At ED triage (13:28), he was classified ESI Level 1 with vitals of BP 88/50, HR 130, RR 24, SpO2 93%, and pain 10/10.

Diagnostic imaging (X-ray and CT angiography) revealed extensive comminuted open segmental fractures of the forearm and hand, a comminuted displaced supracondylar humerus fracture, and complete cessation of contrast enhancement in the brachial artery at the distal third of the humerus, confirming an unsalvageable limb. The emergency physician's impression was a mangled, unsalvageable left upper extremity with complete vascular and neurologic disruption and traumatic shock from acute blood loss and pain. Labs showed leukocytosis (WBC 14.2) and anemia (Hgb 8.9, Hct 27.2); urine drug screen was positive for trace cannabinoids and negative for ethanol. Two units of PRBC were transfused before transfer to the OR.

Dr. Vance performed an emergent left transhumeral (above-elbow) amputation with myofascial closure, bone beveling, and traction-neurectomy of the median, ulnar, and radial nerves; EBL was 650 mL, and a JP drain was placed (removed postoperative day 4, January 12). Postoperative pain management included a Hydromorphone PCA, Gabapentin 300mg PO, Ancef 1g IV, and PRN Oxycodone 5-10mg. Davis was discharged January 15 after a 7-day admission on Gabapentin 300mg TID, Oxycodone 5mg q4-6h PRN, and Cefdinir 300mg BID for 5 more days.

At one-month follow-up (February 12, 2024), the stump was healed but severe phantom limb pain (8/10) and hypersensitivity prompted increasing Gabapentin to 600mg TID and referrals for desensitization therapy and shrinker sock fitting. By June 18, 2024, a tender 1.5cm mobile nodule was identified as a post-amputation traumatic neuroma of the ulnar/median nerve stump, surgically addressed November 12, 2024, when Dr. Vance excised a 1.8 x 1.4 cm neuroma with proximal nerve transposition and embedding into the triceps muscle.

Prosthetic rehabilitation was delayed when Liberty Mutual placed authorization for the proposed myoelectric transhumeral prosthesis on hold pending peer review (December 15, 2024), suspending therapy. Formal PT resumed January 12, 2025, and a custom myoelectric prosthesis (carbon-fiber socket, Utah Myoelectric Elbow, Motion Control MC Hand) was fitted February 5, 2025, with 80% electrode signal accuracy. Over ten documented visits through June 15, 2026, pain declined from 5/10 to 1/10, with two no-shows (May 12 and November 10, 2025) attributed to workload and transportation issues. Davis was discharged June 22, 2026, having achieved master-level prosthetic operation, independent ADLs, driving, carrying up to 25 lbs, and near-normal shoulder ROM, cleared to return to modified light/medium duty at NSK.
